coverage: All twelve local tablets in both English editions: named heroes, divine actors and references, distinct recognizable unnamed roles and selected groups. Source defects and ambiguous divine names are documented separately.

entities.name: Gilgamesh
entities.body: The king of Uruk and the epic’s principal hero, son of Ninsun and Lugalbanda.

entities.name: Enkidu
entities.body: The wild man created by Aruru to match Gilgamesh in strength.

snapshots.body: Gilgamesh’s closest friend and companion, originally a wild man raised among animals.

entities.name: Shamash
entities.body: The sun god, protector of Gilgamesh and Enkidu.

entities.name: Humbaba
entities.body: The fearsome guardian appointed by Enlil to protect the Cedar Forest.

entities.name: Ishtar
entities.body: The goddess of love and war, daughter of Anu and Antum.

entities.name: Utnapishtim
entities.body: Gilgamesh’s distant ancestor, a man granted everlasting life.

entities.name: Ninsun
entities.body: Gilgamesh’s mother, a wise cow-goddess who interprets his dreams.

entities.name: Lugalbanda
entities.body: Gilgamesh’s divine father, invoked as his protector.

entities.name: Shamhat
entities.body: The sex worker from Uruk sent to introduce Enkidu to human society.

entities.name: Siduri
entities.body: The tavern-keeper who lives beside the sea. Also spelled Sirudi here.

entities.name: Urshanabi
entities.body: Utnapishtim’s ferryman, who crosses the Waters of Death. Also spelled Urshinabi here.

entities.name: Anu
entities.body: The sky god and father of Ishtar.

entities.name: Enlil
entities.body: A leading god who exercises authority over humanity and the other gods. Also called Bel here.

entities.name: Ea / Enki
entities.body: The god of wisdom and fresh water, also called Enki and Nudimmud.

entities.name: Aruru
entities.body: The creator goddess who fashions human beings.

entities.name: Adad
entities.body: The god of storms and thunder.

entities.name: Sin
entities.body: The moon god, also invoked as Namra-sit.

entities.name: Ereshkigal
entities.body: The queen of the underworld, also called Irkalla in this edition.

entities.name: Nergal
entities.body: A god associated with death, warfare and the underworld.

entities.name: Ninurta
entities.body: A warrior god who takes part in the gods’ council and the Flood story.

entities.name: Antum
entities.body: Ishtar’s mother and Anu’s consort.

entities.name: The Bull of Heaven
entities.body: The divine bull under Anu’s control, requested by Ishtar.

entities.name: The Anunnaki
entities.body: A collective name for the great gods who determine human fate.

entities.name: The trapper
entities.body: The hunter who encounters Enkidu at the animals’ watering place.

entities.name: The trapper’s father
entities.body: The trapper’s father, whom he consults about Enkidu.

entities.name: The elders of Uruk
entities.body: The city’s senior counselors, who advise Gilgamesh.

entities.name: The scorpion-man
entities.body: One of the guardians of the mountain of Mashu and the sun’s passage.

entities.name: The scorpion-man’s wife
entities.body: The scorpion-man’s wife and fellow guardian at Mount Mashu.

entities.name: The scorpion guardians
entities.body: The beings who guard the entrance to Mount Mashu.

entities.name: The Stone Men
entities.body: Urshanabi’s stone boat crew, immune to the Waters of Death.

entities.name: Utnapishtim’s wife
entities.body: Utnapishtim’s wife, who lives with him at his distant dwelling.

entities.name: The barber
entities.body: The barber who grooms Enkidu as he enters human society.

entities.name: The wedding guest
entities.body: The traveler who explains the wedding customs of Uruk to Enkidu.

entities.name: The figure in Enkidu’s dream
entities.body: The terrifying humanlike figure with animal claws in Enkidu’s dream.

entities.name: The underworld scribe
entities.body: The scribe who reads a tablet before Ereshkigal.

entities.name: The carpenter
entities.body: The carpenter whose shop Gilgamesh recalls in the story of his ball and mallet.

entities.name: The carpenter’s wife
entities.body: The carpenter’s wife, whom Gilgamesh regards as being like a mother.

entities.name: The carpenter’s daughter
entities.body: The carpenter’s daughter, whom Gilgamesh regards as being like a sister.

entities.name: The serpent
entities.body: The snake at the watering place on Gilgamesh’s return journey.

entities.name: Aya
entities.body: The goddess who is Shamash’s consort.

entities.name: Nisaba
entities.body: The grain goddess, invoked in the description of Enkidu’s hair.

entities.name: The Igigi
entities.body: A collective name for a group of gods.

entities.name: Irnina
entities.body: A divine figure associated with victory and the underworld, invoked in Ninsun’s prayer.

entities.name: Irnini
entities.body: The divine name attached to the Cedar Forest’s sanctuary in this translation; printed Imini in the original edition.

entities.name: Ningishzida
entities.body: An underworld god invoked in Ninsun’s prayer.

entities.name: Dumuzi
entities.body: Ishtar’s youthful husband, a shepherd god.

entities.name: The Thunderbird
entities.body: The mighty supernatural bird invoked in the heroes’ dreams and comparisons.

entities.name: The allallu-bird
entities.body: The brightly colored bird named among Ishtar’s former lovers.

entities.name: Silili
entities.body: The mother of the horse named among Ishtar’s former lovers.

entities.name: Ishullanu
entities.body: Anu’s gardener, named among the men desired by Ishtar.

entities.name: The lion
entities.body: The powerful lion named among Ishtar’s former lovers.

entities.name: The horse
entities.body: The warhorse named among Ishtar’s former lovers, offspring of Silili.

entities.name: The shepherd
entities.body: The herdsman named among Ishtar’s former lovers.

entities.name: Etana
entities.body: A legendary king encountered among the inhabitants of the underworld.

entities.name: Shakkan
entities.body: The god of wild animals and herds, named in the underworld vision.

entities.name: Namtar
entities.body: A divine agent of death and disease associated with the underworld.

entities.name: Hushbisha
entities.body: A divine attendant in the court of the underworld.

entities.name: Quassu-tabat
entities.body: A divine attendant of Ereshkigal, honored in the funeral offerings.

entities.name: Ninshuluhha
entities.body: A deity associated with cleaning the underworld’s house.

entities.name: Bibbu
entities.body: A deity serving in the underworld’s court, honored in the funeral offerings.

entities.name: Dumuzi-abzu
entities.body: A separate underworld deity from Ishtar’s husband Dumuzi, named in the funeral offerings.

entities.name: Ubar-Tutu
entities.body: Utnapishtim’s father, also spelled Ubara-Tutu here.

entities.name: Mammitum
entities.body: The goddess who determines human fate with the great gods.

entities.name: Ennugi
entities.body: A god named among the leaders of the divine council.

entities.name: Puzur-Amurri
entities.body: The boatman entrusted with Utnapishtim’s ship in the Flood story.

entities.name: Shullat
entities.body: One of the heralds who accompany the storm god Adad.

entities.name: Hanish
entities.body: One of the heralds who accompany the storm god Adad.

entities.name: Ninazu
entities.body: An underworld god, a son of Ereshkigal in this tradition.

entities.name: Asakku
entities.body: A demon associated with sickness and death.

entities.name: The seven Sages
entities.body: The legendary sages credited with laying the foundations of Uruk’s wall.
